born.why: The code prioritizes survival by eating when starvation is imminent, uses history to avoid known poisons, and employs 'taste' as a low-risk learning strategy for sweet-smelling unknowns when hunger is manageable, balancing data gathering with energy needs.

This code prioritizes survival by immediately rejecting known poisons, carrying known good fruits when possible, and using taste-testing only for sweet-smelling unknowns when hunger allows, balancing data gathering with safety.

The code prioritizes survival by eating anything when extremely hungry, avoids known poisons definitively, learns about new foods via 'taste' only when safe enough (low hunger) and promising (sweet smell), and otherwise leaves risky or low-value items to preserve energy.

The code implements a cautious foraging strategy that prioritizes avoiding known poisons, building a pantry of verified safe foods via 'taste' trials on sweet-smelling unknowns, and only consuming unverified unknowns when hunger is critical or the smell strongly suggests safety.

The code improves survival by prioritizing starvation avoidance, using a recency-weighted scoring system that generalizes safety/poison traits across similar fruits, and distinguishing between 'carry' (for high-confidence safe items) and 'taste' (for uncertain items when hungry) to efficiently update the diary.

The code improves adaptation by using time-decayed memory weights so recent experiences matter more, adjusts thresholds to prevent starvation while avoiding known poison, and distinguishes between carrying (low hunger) and eating/tasting (high hunger) to optimize energy use.
